title: Effect Size and Evaluation of a Physical Group Training Intervention in the Integrative Care of Oncology Patients – A Pilot Study
summary:
This project is a pilot study investigating the feasibility, acceptance, and effect size of weekly group training sessions on selected performance and quality of life parameters in cancer patients. The study aims to establish a foundational data set to support the long term implementation of an oncological exercise supportive program at LMU Klinikum.

Despite robust evidence demonstrating the beneficial effects of structured, needs adapted exercise therapy for oncology patients, many tertiary care hospitals including LMU Klinikum currently lack appropriate infrastructures and program offerings.

This pilot study is integrated within the framework and ongoing successful initiatives of our research group dedicated to implementing exercise therapy in oncology. These initiatives include the multicenter IMPLEMENT study funded by Deutsche Krebshilfe, the multicenter INTEGRATION study funded by the GBA Innovation Fund, the monocentric OPTIMISE study funded by the Jöster Foundation, and the establishment of the working group “Physical Activity in Oncology” at the Comprehensive Cancer Center Munich.

interventions.name: Oncological patients participating in weekly supervised group training sessions
Oncological patients who do not want to participate in a weekly group training.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical clearance for exercise and training eligibility (in cooperation with Med I, LMU Center for Sports Medicine)
Ability to give informed consent at the time of study enrollment and signed informed consent form
Legal adulthood at the time of study enrollment (minimum 18 years old)
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to consent or being underage at the time of study enrollment
- Medical or psychological condition which, in the opinion of the study team, prevents the patient from participating in the study or from providing a legally valid signed informed consent
- Pregnancy
- Existing contraindications to exercise therapy interventions, in particular:
-Clinically manifest heart failure (NYHA class III-IV)
- Therapy-resistant arterial hypertension grade III-IV
- Respiratory insufficiency, severe COPD greater than grade III
- Therapy-resistant thrombocytopenia <10,000/μl, or coagulation disorders with clinically significant increased bleeding risk
- Unstable coronary syndrome or unstable cardiac arrhythmias
-Uncontrolled cerebral epilepsy
- Implanted pacemaker or defibrillator
